definition: The distance around the edge of a circle or round object.

collocations.example: The earth's circumference is about 25,000 miles around the equator.
The nurse measured the circumference of the baby's head carefully.

definition: To limit something or keep it within strict boundaries.

collocations.example: Many strict rules circumscribe daily life in the small village.
The new law will circumscribe the freedom of local businesses.

definition: A loud, ringing sound made when metal is hit.

collocations.example: He pulled the heavy iron gates shut with a loud clang.
The clang of the church bell echoed across the town.

definition: A strong fear of being in small, closed spaces.

collocations.example: Many people suffer from claustrophobia and avoid using crowded elevators.
Small, windowless rooms give me claustrophobia almost right away.

definition: A narrow opening or crack, especially in rock or ground.

collocations.example: The climbers rested in a rocky cleft on the mountainside.
A deep cleft split the surface of the old stone wall.

definition: A short, sharp ringing sound made by glass or metal.

collocations.example: I heard the clink of glasses from the dining room.
The coins fell into the metal tray with a clink.

definition: A covered walkway around an open square in a monastery or college.

collocations.example: The monks walk through the cloister on their way to prayer.
Visitors admired the quiet cloister beside the old cathedral.

definition: To come together to form one larger group or mass.

collocations.example: The small droplets slowly coalesce into larger drops of water.
Several groups began to coalesce around a single shared goal.

definition: A flat brown insect that lives in dirty or warm places.

collocations.example: A cockroach scurries across the kitchen floor at night.
He grabbed a shoe and tried to kill the cockroach.

definition: A silky covering that protects an insect while it grows.

collocations.example: The caterpillar will spin a cocoon before becoming a moth.
A moth slowly emerged from the cocoon on the branch.

definition: The money or funds that a government or organization has available.

collocations.example: The new tax will add millions to the state coffers.
The charity struggled with empty coffers after a difficult year.

definition: To live together as a couple without being married.

collocations.example: Many young couples now choose to cohabit before getting married.
They decided to cohabit for years before planning a wedding.

definition: A natural protein in skin and bones that keeps them firm.

collocations.example: Some skin creams claim to boost collagen and reduce wrinkles.
As we age, our collagen production slowly begins to decrease.

definition: Relating to a college or its students.

collocations.example: She played collegiate sports before turning professional in her twenties.
The national collegiate athletic association governs college sports in America.

definition: The punctuation mark ( , ) used to separate parts of a sentence.

collocations.example: The two clauses are separated by a comma in this sentence.
You should add a comma after the first word here.

definition: A naval officer ranking just above a captain.

collocations.example: After years of service, she was promoted to commodore last spring.
The commodore ordered the fleet to return to the harbor.

definition: The fact of being involved in doing something wrong with others.

collocations.example: Several officers were jailed for their complicity in the crime.
The manager was quick to deny any complicity in the fraud.

definition: To injure someone's brain with a hard blow to the head.

collocations.example: A heavy fall can easily concuss a player during the match.
He slipped and managed to concuss himself on the low ceiling.

definition: To express sympathy to someone who is sad, especially after a death.

collocations.example: We went to condole with him on the loss of his father.
Neighbors came to condole with the family after the funeral.

definition: A person or thing that passes information, money, or goods between others.

collocations.example: The country became a conduit for drugs from across the border.
The assistant acted as a conduit between staff and management.

definition: Pleasant and friendly; easy to get along with.

collocations.example: The cafe has a congenial atmosphere that encourages people to linger.
He relaxed in the congenial company of his old friends.

definition: In agreement with something; matching or consistent.

collocations.example: They want to work for a company whose values are congruent with theirs.
The two teams shared congruent goals and worked well together.

definition: An expert who knows a lot about and enjoys something, such as art or food.

collocations.example: Sarah told me you are something of an art connoisseur.
As a wine connoisseur, he can name a vintage almost instantly.

definition: Agreed to by everyone involved; based on mutual agreement.

collocations.example: The team reached a consensual decision after a long discussion.
I hope we can solve this problem in a consensual way.

definition: An organization that protects nature and the environment.

collocations.example: A nature conservancy bought the land to protect local wildlife.
The farmer agreed to work with the conservancy on the project.

definition: Kind and careful about the feelings and needs of others.

collocations.example: It was very considerate of him to wait for us.
She is always polite and considerate towards her employees.

definition: A feeling of worry, shock, or confusion.

collocations.example: His sudden decision caused consternation among the entire staff.
The fans reacted with consternation to the news of her retirement.

definition: To make it difficult for someone to pass waste from the body.

collocations.example: These rich, fatty foods tend to constipate you if overeaten.
Certain strong painkillers can constipate the patient for several days.

definition: Able to be spread from one person to another, especially a disease.

collocations.example: Scarlet fever is highly contagious and spreads quickly among children.
The clinic isolated patients with a contagious disease to prevent spread.

definition: A substance that makes something dirty, impure, or unsafe.

collocations.example: The filter is designed to remove every contaminant from the water.
Experts tested the soil for any dangerous contaminant near the factory.

definition: Next to or touching something; sharing a border.

collocations.example: The delivery service covers all the contiguous states on the mainland.
Their land is contiguous with the national park to the north.

definition: To twist or bend something out of its normal shape.

collocations.example: The dancer could contort his body into surprising positions.
Pain made her contort her face for a brief moment.

definition: To do something that is not allowed by a law or rule.

collocations.example: The content of the agreement must not contravene the law.
Building here would contravene regulations set by the local council.

definition: The movement of heat through air or liquid as it rises and falls.

collocations.example: Warm convection currents carry heat upward through the atmosphere.
Convection carries warm water to the surface of the pot.

definition: Very complicated and difficult to follow or understand.

collocations.example: Despite its convoluted plot, the novel is a rewarding read.
The refund involves a convoluted process that confuses most customers.

definition: To speak in a soft, gentle, loving voice.

collocations.example: The visitors began to coo over the newborn baby.
She leaned close to coo softly to the sleeping child.

definition: A small cage or enclosure for keeping chickens or other birds.

collocations.example: He built a chicken coop so the family could collect fresh eggs.
The hens settled down in the coop for the night.

definition: In large amounts; plentiful.

collocations.example: She took copious notes during the entire training session.
He drank copious amounts of coffee to stay awake.

definition: Warm and friendly in a polite way.

collocations.example: The two companies have maintained cordial relations for many years.
The staff gave every guest a cordial welcome at the door.

definition: A line of police, soldiers, or barriers that blocks an area.

collocations.example: Demonstrators broke through the police cordon near the building.
Officers formed a cordon between the two angry crowds.

definition: To shape material into a series of folds or ridges.

collocations.example: Factories corrugate the cardboard to make shipping boxes stronger.
Workers corrugate the metal sheets used for the roof.

definition: Something that has an equal but opposite effect to another thing.

collocations.example: The committee acts as a counterbalance to the director's power.
Her calm nature was a useful counterbalance to his quick temper.

definition: A car with a fixed roof and usually two doors.

collocations.example: He parked his new sports coupe outside the office building.
She prefers to drive a small coupe through the city.

definition: To crouch or move back because of fear.

collocations.example: The puppy began to cower in fear during the storm.
The children would cower behind the sofa during loud thunder.

definition: Unwilling to give information; shy or pretending to be shy.

collocations.example: She was rather coy about how much her dress cost.
He gave me a coy smile and said nothing more.

definition: A wild animal like a small wolf, found in North America.

collocations.example: Late at night, a coyote howled somewhere up the canyon.
Hikers often spot a coyote crossing the dry desert trail.

definition: A small, sour red berry used in sauces and juice.

collocations.example: We always serve cranberry sauce with the turkey at Thanksgiving.
She drinks a glass of cranberry juice every morning.

definition: A stick of colored wax used for drawing.

collocations.example: The child colored the picture with a bright red crayon.
He gave his daughter a box of crayons for her birthday.

definition: Belief that something is true or that someone can be trusted.

collocations.example: The new evidence lends credence to his original theory.
They refused to give credence to the findings of the survey.

definition: A narrow crack or opening, especially in rock.

collocations.example: The small lizard disappeared into a rock crevice near the path.
Tiny plants grew in a crevice on the old stone wall.

definition: A small bed with high sides for a baby.

collocations.example: The newborn sleeps in a crib beside her parents' bed.
She gently put the baby in the crib for a nap.

definition: To form, or cause to form, many small folds or creases.

collocations.example: Please do not crinkle the paper when you wrap the gift.
She would crinkle her nose whenever she smelled something odd.

definition: A close friend or companion, often one who gets unfair favors.

collocations.example: He spent the evening drinking with an old crony from work.
The mayor gave the best jobs to his cronies.

definition: To sing or speak in a soft, gentle voice.

collocations.example: The mother began to croon a lullaby to her baby.
The singer would croon softly into the old microphone.

definition: A word puzzle where you write answers in a grid of squares.

collocations.example: She likes to do a crossword with her morning coffee.
He could not finish the crossword puzzle in today's newspaper.

definition: To criticize or punish someone very harshly.

collocations.example: My boss will crucify me if this report is late.
The politician was crucified by the press after the scandal.

definition: The most important or difficult part of a problem.

collocations.example: Now we finally come to the crux of the matter.
Funding is the crux of the problem we face today.

definition: An underground room beneath a church, often used for burials.

collocations.example: The famous writer is buried in the crypt below the cathedral.
A narrow stone staircase leads down to the crypt.

definition: Having a hidden meaning; mysterious and hard to understand.

collocations.example: He left a cryptic message that nobody could fully understand.
She issued a short, cryptic statement denying the charges.

definition: Made of crystals or having their regular structure.

collocations.example: Salt forms a regular crystalline structure when it dries out.
Sugar is a crystalline solid that dissolves easily in water.

definition: Deserving blame for something bad that happened.

collocations.example: Many now see him as culpable for the whole crisis.
The company was held culpable for the serious safety failures.

definition: The moving mark on a computer screen showing where you are typing.

collocations.example: He moved the cursor across the screen and clicked the icon.
Position the cursor where you want the new text to begin.

definition: Done quickly and without attention to detail.

collocations.example: He cast a cursory glance at the menu, then closed it.
A cursory inspection failed to reveal the hidden damage.

definition: A person who is responsible for taking care of something.

collocations.example: The museum is the custodian of many priceless paintings.
Every record has a data custodian who ensures its accuracy.

definition: Shaped like a cylinder, with straight sides and round ends.

collocations.example: The storage tank is cylindrical in shape and very tall.
They packed the samples into a small cylindrical container.

definition: To do something casually or without serious commitment.

collocations.example: In my free time, I started to dabble in software development.
He likes to dabble with painting on the weekends.

definition: A yellow spring flower with a trumpet-shaped center.

collocations.example: A single wild daffodil bloomed at the edge of the field.
She planted daffodil bulbs in the garden last autumn.

definition: Silly or foolish.

collocations.example: Driving all the way there in this storm is a daft idea.
I know this might sound daft, but let me explain.

definition: Small, delicate, and pretty.

collocations.example: She served a dainty cake decorated with tiny sugar flowers.
The child picked up the beads with her dainty fingers.

definition: The panel of controls and dials in front of a car driver.

collocations.example: The clock on the dashboard said it was almost two.
He twiddled a knob on the dashboard to adjust the heat.

definition: A complete and often embarrassing failure.

collocations.example: Many people lost money during the whole financial debacle.
The launch event turned into a complete debacle for the company.

definition: Based on the number ten; counted or divided in tens.

collocations.example: Move the decimal point two places to the right.
The figure is accurate to two decimal places.

definition: To destroy a large part of something.

collocations.example: The disease could decimate the local bird population within weeks.
The budget cuts would decimate basic services for the needy.

definition: A person or thing used to lead someone away or trick them.

collocations.example: One officer would play decoy while the others moved in.
Marketers use the decoy effect to guide customer choices.

definition: A very large number of things that arrive at the same time.

collocations.example: The office received a deluge of requests for interviews.
The new policy brought a deluge of complaints from customers.

definition: To mark or fix the boundary or limits of something.

collocations.example: A special commission was formed to demarcate the border.
Fences were built to demarcate the boundary between the two farms.

definition: To make someone or something seem less worthy of respect.

collocations.example: Such advertisements clearly demean women and should be removed.
I would not demean myself by begging for the job.

definition: To move someone to a lower position or rank.

collocations.example: It is unfair to demote an employee without a clear reason.
The board voted to demote the manager after poor results.

definition: To criticize someone or something unfairly to make them seem bad.

collocations.example: I did not intend to denigrate her achievements in any way.
He would never denigrate the work of his talented colleagues.

definition: The number below the line in a fraction.

collocations.example: To add these fractions, they must share a common denominator.
You divide the top number by the denominator below it.

definition: To stop a process or plan from continuing as intended.

collocations.example: This latest incident could derail the entire peace process.
A single disagreement threatened to derail the trade talks.

definition: The branch of medicine dealing with the skin and its diseases.

collocations.example: She decided to study dermatology after finishing medical school.
He works as a nurse at a busy dermatology clinic.

definition: Very sad and without hope.

collocations.example: She was becoming increasingly despondent about her job search.
He felt despondent over the breakup of his marriage.

definition: A ruler who has total power and uses it unfairly.

collocations.example: The country was ruled for decades by a cruel despot.
He ran the small company like a despot.

definition: Extremely poor and without the basic things needed to live.

collocations.example: When he died, his family was left completely destitute.
After the flood, many families were left utterly destitute.

definition: Using dishonest or indirect methods to get what you want.

collocations.example: He became rich through devious means and clever lies.
They came up with a devious plan to avoid paying.

definition: The muscle below the lungs that helps you breathe.

collocations.example: The diaphragm contracts and pulls air into the lungs.
Singers learn to breathe from the diaphragm for better control.

definition: To change information into a digital form that a computer can use.

collocations.example: The hospital plans to digitise all of its paper records.
The library received funds to digitise its rare book collection.

definition: An important official or person with a high rank.

collocations.example: A foreign dignitary visited the factory during the official tour.
Security was tight for the visiting dignitaries at the summit.

definition: Old and in very bad condition.

collocations.example: They finally bought the dilapidated building in order to restore it.
The walls of the dilapidated shed leaned outward dangerously.

definition: To become, or make something become, wider or larger.

collocations.example: In the dark, our pupils dilate to let in more light.
Red wine can help to dilate the blood vessels slightly.

definition: Extremely small.

collocations.example: She was a diminutive figure standing beside her tall husband.
Despite its diminutive size, the dog was surprisingly brave.

definition: A small hollow on the skin, especially in the cheek when smiling.

collocations.example: A dimple forms on her cheek when she smiles.
You have a very cute dimple in your cheek.

definition: A small open boat.

collocations.example: They crossed the calm bay in a small rubber dinghy.
The sailors spent hours adrift in a dinghy before rescue.
